He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]]. ==High school career== Sims played for [[Mount Saint Joseph High School (Baltimore)|Mt. Saint Joseph High]] averaging 19 points and 13 rebounds as a senior. He led his team to three BCL and MIAA Championships and earned Player of the Year and All Metro honors.{{cite web|url=http://www.guhoyas.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/sims_henry00.html|title=14 Henry Sims|work=GUHoyas.com|access-date=September 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924024123/http://www.guhoyas.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/sims_henry00.html|archive-date=September 24, 2015|url-status=dead}} ==College career== Sims played for four years at [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] where he played in 104 games, starting 17, averaging 3.8 points, 2.6 rebounds. He had his best year as a senior, averaging 11.6 points, 6.0 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game connecting on 46.3 percent of his field goals.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/henry-sims-1.html |title=Henry Sims Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=November 25, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119130615/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/henry-sims-1.html |archive-date=November 19, 2015 }} ==Professional career== ===Erie BayHawks (2012–2013)=== After going undrafted in the 2012 NBA draft, Sims joined the [[Utah Jazz]] for the Orlando Summer League and [[Chicago Bulls]] for the Las Vegas Summer League.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-announce-2012-summer-league-roster.html|title=BULLS ANNOUNCE 2012 SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2012|access-date=September 16, 2015}} On September 10, 2012, he signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Henry-Sims/Summary/2371|title=Henry Sims Player Profile – RealGM|work=RealGM.com|access-date=September 16, 2015}} However, he was waived on October 27.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11312|title=Knicks waive Oscar Bellfield, John Shurna, Mychel Thompson, Henry Sims|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 27, 2012|access-date=September 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029201607/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11312|archive-date=October 29, 2013|url-status=dead}} In November 2012, he was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]]. On February 4, 2013, Sims was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |title=2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced |work=NBA.com |date=February 4, 2013 |access-date=September 16, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022065410/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |archive-date=October 22, 2013 }} ===New Orleans Hornets / Erie BayHawks / Petron Blaze Boosters (2013)=== On March 3, 2013, Sims signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/99643/hornets-sign-henry-sims-to-a-10-day-contract.html|title=Hornets sign Henry Sims to a 10-day contract|work=Sportando.com|date=March 3, 2013|access-date=September 16, 2015}} He appeared in two games for the Hornets recording a total of four points and two rebounds. He was released by the Hornets on March 12, 2013{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/99827/hornets-sign-lou-amundson-release-henry-sims.html|title=Hornets sign Lou Amundson, release Henry Sims|work=Sportando.com|date=March 12, 2013|access-date=September 16, 2015}} and returned to the BayHawks. On April 1, 2013, his contract was bought out by the BayHawks, and a day later, signed with the [[Petron Blaze Boosters]] of the Philippines.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cat/nba/100227/henry-sims-signs-with-petron-blaze-in-the-philippines.html|title=Henry Sims signs with Petron Blaze in the Philippines|work=Sportando.com|date=April 2, 2013|access-date=September 16, 2015}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2013–2014)=== He joined the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On September 30, 2013, he signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. On December 5, 2013, he was assigned to the [[Canton Charge]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/assign-felix-sims-131205|title=Cavs Assign Sims and Felix to Charge|work=NBA.com|date=December 5, 2013|access-date=September 16, 2015}} He was recalled by the Cavaliers on December 9.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-felix-sims-131209|title=Cavs Recall Felix and Sims|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2013|access-date=September 16, 2015}} On December 11, he was reassigned to Canton.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/assign-felix-sims-karasev-131211|title=Cavs Assign Felix, Karasev and Sims to Charge|work=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2013|access-date=September 16, 2015}} He was recalled the next day. ===Philadelphia 76ers (2014–2015)=== On February 20, 2014, Sims was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] along with [[Earl Clark]] and two future second-round picks in exchange for [[Spencer Hawes]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-acquire-two-second-round-picks-2014-nba-draft-cleveland-cavaliers|title=Sixers Acquire Two Second-Round Picks in 2014 NBA Draft From Cleveland Cavaliers|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2014|access-date=September 16, 2015}} On March 22, 2014, Sims recorded 18 points and a career high 15 rebounds in an 81–91 loss to the Chicago Bulls.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140322/PHICHI/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Bulls 91, 76ers 81|work=NBA.com|date=March 22,
